subject: treasureHoard
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: treasure hoard: coins, gems, chest, crown, goblets.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static treasure hoard model — an open chest, merged coin heaps, glowing gem shapes, a crown, and goblets — built from basic geometries, lathes, and extrusions with glow effects, all staying in model space since no joints are needed.

I'm going for a League of Legends-style painterly look with saturated gold, blue hextech glow, and metal paint, possibly reusing the clockwork kit's metal material or crafting my own. I'm working out the chest's layout and dimensions, with a paneled wood base, gold bands, and a hinged lid built from an extruded half-disc profile oriented so it opens backward convincingly.

Still working out the lid hinge geometry...

Computing the thickness direction via cross product confirms the extrude setup works symmetrically, so I can proceed defining the lid outline as a barrel profile: a rectangle base with an arced dome top traced through u-v points.

For the gold bands, I'll reuse this outline but scale it slightly larger around the profile's center by a growth factor, giving thin raised trim without building a separate shape.

Now I'm laying out the chest body itself: a box for the base, a hinge point at the back for the lid, gold trim bands positioned using the offset outline, corner studs, a front lock plate with a glowing gem, and feet underneath. For the interior, I'm planning a heap-of-coins generator that scatters tilted cylinders into a mound shape to simulate a treasure pile.

For the coin heaps I'm computing a parabolic height profile so coins sit naturally on a mound, randomizing position and tilt within a disc, and merging around 450 small coin cylinders (8-segment, low-poly) into a few geometries grouped by gold color variant to keep part count low while staying under a reasonable triangle budget.

For gems I'm using flat-shaded icosahedrons and stretched octahedrons in ruby, sapphire, emerald, and amethyst, each given a glow pass, scattered across the heaps and merged by color group using the heap height function for placement.

For goblets I'm building lathe-profile geometry (foot, stem, bowl) in gold with a jeweled band, placing two upright and one tipped over on its side with spilled coins nearby, rotating the tipped one around a near-horizontal axis so it rests convincingly on the floor.

Now I'm designing the crown: a lathe-generated band ring with cone-shaped spikes for points, gold gem-tipped cones, and larger gems set into the band, positioned on top of the coin pile.

Skipping swords and scrolls, I'll add a hextech-style gold plaque decal on the chest with a textured plane for the emblem, plus a few standing coins using textured circle geometry to simulate embossed faces.

For materials, I'm giving gold a gilt metal look and wood a deep teal-blue grain ("#2a3e5c") with gold trim for a Demacian/Hextech feel, instead of plain brown. For the ground, the coin heaps serve as the base itself, so I need a flattened cone or lathe shape underneath to give the mounds solid support.

Defining mound geometry...

I'll scale down the mound radius slightly and scatter extra coins to fill the chest rim without clipping walls, placing a crown on heap A's peak and working out goblet positions—one upright on the floor, one upright further left, and one tipped over on heap B.

Now I'm defining the goblet's radial profile as a lathe shape, building the outer wall up to the rim and the inner wall back down to the cup floor so the mesh closes properly at the axis.

The outline closes properly along the axis with smoothing disabled and 10 segments. Now I'm planning gem placement: a helper function to ring gems around the goblet bowl at a given radius and height, collecting them into color-grouped lists for merging and glow effects later, plus a generic addGem helper for position/size/color/rotation. For the crown I'm adding cone-shaped spikes around the band with alternating heights and gem-tipped spheres, feeding into the same gem collection system.

Shaping the lathe profile for the crown band and velvet cap with tapered outer/inner points, then placing 8 gems around the crown band at a small size.

Now I'm thinking through merging geometries safely: Icosahedron and Octahedron gems are non-indexed, while cylinders and cones used for coins and crown parts are indexed, so I need to group merges by matching attribute type rather than mixing them carelessly.

Setting up coin colors and flat shading: I'll use flat gold tones (#f2c23a, #e0a82a, #ffd96a) for coins without needing paint/UV textures, and a brown mound color (#9c6a1e), keeping well under the 64-color limit.

Writing the heap generation function...

I'm also adding coin stacks near the front with slight random offsets, scattering gems across each heap with randomized sizes, and placing a few larger stretched gems in front using octahedron geometry.

For the gems, I'm assigning a jewel-tone palette (ruby, sapphire, emerald, amethyst, citrine, aqua) with strong glow, and for the chest I'm building the wooden base box with grain-based surface painting, adding gold bands around the width, and placing small corner studs.

I'm adding the top and bottom gold trim rims, then working out the front lock plate position and an emblem plane with a hexagonal star design, deciding to skip the lock since it overlaps the lid area and keep the emblem glow modest. Now I'm moving on to designing the lid.

Still computing hinge rotation geometry...

Still refining outline geometry...

I'm deciding to skip hinges and inner lining details for simplicity, and checking that the open lid's top position and back lean still fit within the scene bounds. For remaining elements I'm thinking about adding sparkle star cards near the gems, using a white four-point star on gold as a simple SVG texture.

I'm working out the orientation for sparkle cards and other textures—emblem, coin, sparkle, maybe a rune motif on the goblet—then moving to the crown placement using a quaternion built from Euler angles to orient the lathe axis correctly.

For the goblets, I'm computing a tilt direction and deriving a quaternion with setFromUnitVectors to orient a tipped goblet, then writing a generic goblet function that places the lathe body and gem ring consistently using position and rotation. I'm assigning materials—gilt gold for one, a silvery tone for the other.

I'm sketching out the chest's wood grain paint, a gem cluster sitting atop the coin mound inside the chest, and recording gem positions for later sparkle effects, then moving into merging transformed geometries by color using a map keyed by color string.

Now I'm shaping octahedron gem geometry with transform matrices, assembling the static chest part without joints since it doesn't need bones, and confirming the chest base sits flush with the ground.
